This term means 'common' or 'ordinary.' It is often used to describe something that is shared or should not be kept secret. In the context of this verse, it evokes the idea that Jesus' miracles, while extraordinary, should remain within the realm of personal revelation rather than being exposed to the public, thus highlighting the sacred nature of his ministry.

This verb means 'to make evident' or 'to declare clearly.' It is used to describe the action of making something manifest or known. In this verse, it highlights the contrast between Jesus' instruction to keep silent and the human tendency to proclaim what is perceived as extraordinary, shedding light on the difficulty of following divine instructions in a world eager for sensationalism.

36.epoque: This passage is set in the first century, during Jesus' earthly ministry in Palestine, a period marked by Roman occupation and messianic expectation among the Jewish people.
36.passage: In Mark 7, Jesus performs miracles, including the healing of a deaf-mute. This chapter illustrates his compassion and divine authority while addressing the tensions between religious traditions and the truth revealed by Christ.
36.culture: The Jewish culture of the time valued discretion and honor but was also plagued by messianic expectations that drove people to seek signs and wonders. This creates a context where Jesus' instructions to keep silent may seem paradoxical.
36.interpretation: This verse reveals the complexity of Jesus' mission, which seeks to avoid popularity based on miracles. It also highlights the human nature of wanting to share good news, even when it goes against divine instructions, illustrating the struggle between obedience and the desire for proclamation.
36.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of obedience to God's will, even when our natural inclination is to share our extraordinary experiences. We are called to live our faith authentically, testifying to Christ's work in our lives while respecting divine timing and instructions. It encourages us to seek a personal relationship with God rather than seeking human recognition.

mots.sens: This word means 'wonderful' or 'astonishing'. It comes from the root 'θαυμάζω' (thaumazo), which means 'to be amazed' or 'to marvel'. In this context, it emphasizes the extraordinary nature of Jesus' miracles, revealing his divinity and authority over creation. Theologically, it reminds us that Jesus is the one who transforms the impossible into the possible.

This term refers to a person who is deaf or mute. It is derived from the root 'κωφός', which evokes silence or the inability to speak. In the context of this verse, it highlights Jesus' power to restore communication, both physical and spiritual, symbolizing the redemption and healing that Christ brings to those who are spiritually deaf and mute.

This verb means 'to speak' or 'to express oneself'. It is often used in the New Testament to refer to the proclamation of God's word. In this verse, it underscores the restored ability to communicate, which is a symbol of the liberation and new life that Jesus offers to those who believe in him.

37.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Jesus' ministry in Galilee, at a time when he performed many miracles to prove his divine authority and messianic role.
37.passage: In Mark 7, Jesus is outside of Israel, and he heals a deaf-mute, demonstrating his power over diseases and his compassion for all, regardless of their origin or social status.
37.culture: At this time, physical illnesses were often perceived as signs of sin or curse. The healing of the deaf and mute was particularly significant, as it symbolized a complete restoration of dignity and communication.
37.interpretation: This verse reminds us that Jesus is capable of restoring not only bodies but also souls. He invites us to recognize our own inability to hear and speak spiritually without him, and to seek his healing and transformation.
37.commentaire: This passage encourages us to be witnesses of the wonders that Jesus performs in our lives. Like the witnesses of this miracle, we are called to proclaim the works of God and to share the hope of healing and restoration that Christ offers to all. Let us be attentive to his voice and ready to testify to his goodness.
